label: thm:gkz
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: thm:general
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:general}
Assume \eqref{eq:intro-support}. There is a finite stratification of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ by locally closed algebraic subsets on which the multiplicities of $\operatorname{CC}^L(M_b)$ along $\Lambda_1,\ldots,\Lambda_q$ are simultaneously constant. Moreover, each multiplicity is Zariski upper semicontinuous on the closed points of $\operatorname{Spec} B$.
head: environment

label: thm:gkz-app
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:gkz-app}
Under the assumptions on $A$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:gkz}, the functions
\[
\beta\longmapsto d_s(M_A(\beta)), \quad \beta\longmapsto e_\rho(M_A(\beta))
\]
are Zariski upper semicontinuous for every real $s>1$ and $\rho>1$. Moreover, the second function is zero if $\rho\notin\Sigma(A,Y)$, and the levels used to define $e_\rho$ may be chosen independently of $\beta$.
head: environment

label: def:projective-filtration
title: Definition
head: environment

label: def:rees-good-filtration
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:rees-good-filtration}
The \emph{Rees algebra} of $D_B$ is
\[
\mathscr R_B=\operatorname{Rees}_LD_B=\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}F_k^LD_B\,h^k\subseteq D_B[h,h^{-1}].
\]
For a finite $D_B$-module $M$ with a filtration $F_\bullet M$ compatible with $F_\bullet^LD_B$, its \emph{Rees module} is
\[
\mathscr M=\operatorname{Rees}_FM=\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}F_kM\,h^k\subseteq M[h,h^{-1}].
\]
The filtration is \emph{good} if $\mathscr M$ is finite over $\mathscr R_B$.
head: environment

label: def:characteristic-cycle
title: Definition
head: environment

label: lem:basechange
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: After inverting $h$, the tensor product $N$ becomes $M'[h,h^{-1}]$. The image of $N$ in this localization has degree-$k$ part equal to the image of $F_kM\otimes_BB'$ in $M'$, multiplied by $h^k$. It is therefore the Rees module of the stated filtration. The kernel of the localization map is $H^0_{(h)}N$, which proves \eqref{eq:basechange-rees}. Since $N$ is finite over $\mathscr R_{B'}$, its image is finite, and the filtration is good. Passing to the quotient by $h$ gives \eqref{eq:basechange-surj} by right exactness. If $B'$ is flat, the injectivity of multiplication by $h$ on $\mathscr M$ is preserved, and $H^0_{(h)}N=0$.
head: environment

label: def:relative-support
title: Definition
head: environment

label: rem:filtration-choice
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:filtration-choice}
The support condition \eqref{eq:product-support} is imposed on a good filtration of the relative module $M$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:basechange}, the induced filtrations on the fibers are good and satisfy the same support condition. The multiplicities in \eqref{eq:mu-family} are independent of the choice of good filtration on each fiber.
head: environment

label: ex:bad-support
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:bad-support}
Let $R=\mathbb C[t]_{(t)}$, take one differential variable $x$, and use the order filtration. Consider
\[
M=D_R/D_R(t\partial_x-1).
\]
Over $K$, this is a rank-one connection, whereas $M/tM=0$. This family occurs in \cite[Remark~2.7]{MMW05}. Its relative associated graded module has support $V(t\xi)$: since the associated graded ring is a domain, the initial ideal of the principal left ideal is generated by $t\xi$. Over $t=0$ this support contains the entire cotangent plane. It is therefore not contained in a product with a fixed finite union of curves. This explains why fiberwise holonomicity alone does not give the hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:general}.

label: thm:curve
title: Theorem

label: lem:nilpotent
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:nilpotent-exact
title: Proof
body_md:
There is an exact sequence of modules annihilated by $z$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nilpotent-exact}
0\longrightarrow0:_{zV}z\longrightarrow0:_Vz\longrightarrow V/zV
\xrightarrow{\ z\ }zV/z^2V\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
To verify exactness, first observe that the kernel of the natural map $0:_Vz\to V/zV$ is $(0:_Vz)\cap zV=0:_{zV}z$. If $v+zV$ belongs to the kernel of multiplication by $z$ on $V/zV$, then $zv=z^2w$ for some $w\in V$. Hence $v-zw\in0:_Vz$, and its image in $V/zV$ is $v+zV$. Finally, the map $V/zV\to zV/z^2V$ is surjective by definition. This proves the exactness of \eqref{eq:nilpotent-exact}.


Additivity in \eqref{eq:nilpotent-exact} gives
\[
[0:_Vz]-[V/zV]=[0:_{zV}z]-[zV/z^2V].
\]
Repeat this equality for $zV,z^2V,\ldots,z^{a-1}V$. The last difference is zero, proving \eqref{eq:nilpotent-class}.
head: environment

label: lem:two-parameters
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $N$ is Noetherian, the ascending chain
\[
0:_Nh\subseteq0:_Nh^2\subseteq\cdots
\]
stabilizes. Thus $h^aU=0$ for some $a\ge1$. If $hn\in U$, then $h^{a+1}n=0$, so $n\in U$. It follows that $U\cap hN=hU$ and that $V=N/U$ has no $h$-torsion. Consequently, reducing the exact sequence $0\to U\to N\to V\to0$ modulo $h$ gives
\[
0\longrightarrow U/hU\longrightarrow N/hN
\longrightarrow V/hV\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since $N/hN\simeq G/tG$, this proves \eqref{eq:two-exact}.



We next prove \eqref{eq:two-kernels}. Let $\bar a\in0:_Nh$ be represented by $a\in\mathscr Q$. Since $h\bar a=0$, there exists $b\in\mathscr Q$ such that $ha=tb$. Moreover, $b$ is unique because multiplication by $t$ is injective on $\mathscr Q$. Define a map $0:_Nh\to0:_Gt$ by sending $\bar a$ to the class $\bar b$ of $b$ in $G$. If $a$ is replaced by $a+td$, then $b$ is replaced by $b+hd$, so the map is well defined. If $\bar b=0$, then $b=hd$ for some $d\in\mathscr Q$. Hence $h(a-td)=0$, and the injectivity of $h$ gives $a=td$. This proves injectivity. Conversely, given $\bar b\in0:_Gt$, we have $tb=ha$ for some $a\in\mathscr Q$. The class of $a$ in $N$ belongs to $0:_Nh$ and maps to $\bar b$, proving surjectivity. Since $t$ and $h$ are central, the map is linear over $\mathscr A/(t,h)$.



Since $V=N/U$ has no $h$-torsion, we have $0:_Nh=0:_Uh$. As $h^aU=0$ for some $a\ge1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:nilpotent} gives $[U/hU]=[0:_Uh]$. Taking equivalence classes in \eqref{eq:two-exact} and using \eqref{eq:two-kernels}, we obtain \eqref{eq:two-class}.
head: environment

label: def:local-euler-characteristic
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:local-euler-characteristic}
Let $V$ be a finite module over a Noetherian local ring, and suppose that the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by $t$ on $V$ have finite length. The \emph{Euler characteristic of multiplication by $t$} is
\[
\chi_t(V)=\ell(V/tV)-\ell(0:_Vt).
\]
head: environment
name: Local Euler characteristic

label: lem:local-euler
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:local-euler}
Let $G$ be a finite $W_R$-module satisfying
\[
\operatorname{Supp} G\subseteq\bigcup_i V(P_iW_R).
\]
Then the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by $t$ on $G_{\mathfrak q_i}$ have finite length, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-euler}
\ell(G_{\mathfrak q_i}/tG_{\mathfrak q_i})
-\ell(0:_{G_{\mathfrak q_i}}t)
=\ell_{(W_R)_{\mathfrak p_i}}G_{\mathfrak p_i}. 
\end{equation}
head: environment

label: eq:component-dvr
title: Proof
body_md:
If $P_jW_R\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$, then contraction to $W$ gives $P_j\subseteq P_i$. The ideals $P_i$ define distinct irreducible subvarieties of the same dimension, so $j=i$. Thus only the component indexed by $i$ survives in the support after localization at $\mathfrak q_i$.


The ring
\begin{equation}\label{eq:component-dvr}
\left((W/P_i)\otimes_\mathbb C R\right)_{(t)}
\end{equation}
is a domain because $W/P_i$ is geometrically integral over $\mathbb C$ and $(W/P_i)\otimes_\mathbb C R$ embeds into the domain $(W/P_i)\otimes_\mathbb C K$. It is a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal is generated by the nonzero element $t$, and hence a discrete valuation ring \cite[Tag~00PD]{Stacks}. Its residue field is $\operatorname{Frac}(W/P_i)$, and its only prime ideals are $(0)$ and $(t)$. By the support condition and the preceding argument, the only possible primes in $\operatorname{Supp} G_{\mathfrak q_i}$ are $\mathfrak p_i(W_R)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ and $\mathfrak q_i(W_R)_{\mathfrak q_i}$.


Write $A_i=(W_R)_{\mathfrak q_i}$. By the existence of finite prime filtrations \cite[Tag~00L0]{Stacks}, $G_{\mathfrak q_i}$ has a finite filtration whose successive quotients are isomorphic to
\[
A_i/\mathfrak p_iA_i
\quad\text{or}\quad A_i/\mathfrak q_iA_i.
\]
On a factor of the first type, multiplication by $t$ is injective, with cokernel of length one. On a factor of the second type, its kernel and cokernel both have length one. Thus all the required lengths are finite.

By the kernel--cokernel exact sequence for multiplication by $t$, the Euler characteristic $\chi_t$ is additive on short exact sequences of modules with this support. Hence $\chi_t(G_{\mathfrak q_i})$ equals the number of factors of the first type. Localizing the prime filtration at $\mathfrak p_i$ annihilates every factor of the second type, while each factor of the first type becomes the residue field of $(W_R)_{\mathfrak p_i}$. It follows that $\chi_t(G_{\mathfrak q_i})=\ell_{(W_R)_{\mathfrak p_i}}G_{\mathfrak p_i}$, as claimed.
head: environment

label: prop:torsionfree-constant
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $i$, combining \eqref{eq:defect-length} with Lemma~\ref{lem:local-euler}, we obtain $\mu_i(Q/tQ)=\ell_{(W_R)_{\mathfrak p_i}}G_{\mathfrak p_i}$. Since $R\to K$ is a localization, Lemma~\ref{lem:basechange} gives
\[
G\otimes_RK=\operatorname{gr}_F(Q_K).
\]
Moreover, $(W_R)_{\mathfrak p_i}=(W_K)_{P_iW_K}$, so $\ell_{(W_R)_{\mathfrak p_i}}G_{\mathfrak p_i}=\mu_i(Q_K)$. This proves \eqref{eq:torsionfree-cycle}.
head: environment

label: ex:rees-defect
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:rees-defect}
Let $R=\mathbb C[t]_{(t)}$ and let $Q=R[x]$ have its usual $D_R$-module structure. Choose positive integers $a,m$. The submodule
\[
\mathscr Q=(t^a,h^m)R[x,h]\subseteq Q[h,h^{-1}]
\]
is the Rees module of a good order filtration on $Q$. It is stable under $x$ and $h\partial_x$, and becomes all of $Q[h,h^{-1}]$ after $h$ is inverted. Let $e_0=t^a$ and $e_1=h^m$. These generators satisfy $h^me_0=t^ae_1$ over $R[x,h]$. Hence, with grading shifts suppressed,
\[
G=\mathscr Q/h\mathscr Q\simeq R[x]e_0\oplus(R/(t^a))[x]e_1,
\]
and
\[
N=\mathscr Q/t\mathscr Q\simeq\mathbb C[x,h]/(h^m)e_0\oplus\mathbb C[x,h]e_1.
\]
The order symbol $\xi$ kills $G$, so the product support condition holds with the zero section. The $h$-torsion of $N$ is its first summand. At the generic point of the zero section of the special fiber,
\[
\ell(G/tG)=2,
\quad\ell(0:_Gt)=1,
\quad\ell(U/hU)=1.
\]
Since $Q_K$ and $Q/tQ$ both have multiplicity one, \eqref{eq:defect-length} reads $2-1=1$. The natural surjection from $G/tG$ to $\operatorname{gr}_F(Q/tQ)$ has a nonzero kernel even though $Q$ is flat over $R$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Noetherianity, $T=H^0_{(t)}M$ is a finite submodule of $M$ annihilated by some power $t^a$. Equip $T$ with the induced good filtration and $Q=M/T$ with the quotient filtration. Their associated graded modules satisfy the product
support condition \eqref{eq:product-support}.

Since $Q$ is torsion-free over the discrete valuation ring $R$, it is $R$-flat \cite[Tag~0539]{Stacks}. Tensoring $0\to T\to M\to Q\to0$ with $k$ therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:special-torsion-exact}
0\longrightarrow T/tT\longrightarrow M/tM\longrightarrow Q/tQ\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Since $M_K=Q_K$, additivity of characteristic cycles and Proposition~\ref{prop:torsionfree-constant} give
\[
\operatorname{CC}^L(M/tM)-\operatorname{sp}_\Lambda\operatorname{CC}^L(M_K)=\operatorname{CC}^L(T/tT).
\]

The free resolution $0\to R\xrightarrow{t}R\to k\to0$ gives
\[
\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,k)=0:_Mt=0:_Tt.
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:nilpotent} with $z=t$ to $T$. The modules in its exact sequences are finite $D_R/(t)$-modules. With induced or quotient filtrations, their associated graded supports are contained in $\Lambda$, so characteristic cycles define an additive invariant on them. We conclude that
\[
\operatorname{CC}^L(T/tT)=\operatorname{CC}^L(0:_Tt)=\operatorname{CC}^L\bigl(\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,k)\bigr).
\]
Every coefficient of this last cycle is a nonnegative length. This proves \eqref{eq:curve-tor} and the asserted inequalities.
head: environment

label: cor:flat-curve
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:flat-curve}
If $M$ is $R$-flat and satisfies the product support condition \eqref{eq:product-support}, its generic and special $L$-characteristic cycles have the same coefficients on the fixed components.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Flatness makes $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,k)$ vanish, so the assertion follows from \eqref{eq:curve-tor}.
head: environment

label: cor:flatness
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:flatness}
Assume \eqref{eq:product-support} for the order filtration. Then
\[
M_R\text{ is }R\text{-flat}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{CC}^F(M_R/tM_R)=\operatorname{sp}_\Lambda\operatorname{CC}^F(M_R\otimes_RK).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The module $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,k)$ is finite over $D$, and its induced good order filtration has characteristic support contained in $\Lambda$. Hence it is holonomic. A nonzero holonomic module has a nonempty characteristic variety of dimension $n$, with positive multiplicities \cite[Chapter~3]{HTT08}. By Theorem~\ref{thm:curve}, equality of the cycles is therefore equivalent to $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,k)=0$. Since $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,k)=0:_{M_R}t$, its vanishing is equivalent to torsion-freeness and hence to flatness over $R$ \cite[Tag~0539]{Stacks}.
head: environment

label: ex:rank-flatness
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:rank-flatness}
Let $R=\mathbb C[t]_{(t)}$ and $\delta_0=D_{\mathbb A^1}/D_{\mathbb A^1}x$. The family
\[
M_R=(R\otimes_\mathbb C\mathcal O_{\mathbb A^1})\oplus((R/(t))\otimes_\mathbb C\delta_0)
\]
has rank one on both fibers, whereas their characteristic cycles for the order filtration are $[T^*_{\mathbb A^1}\mathbb A^1]$ and $[T^*_{\mathbb A^1}\mathbb A^1]+[T_0^*\mathbb A^1]$, respectively. Its first Tor module is $\delta_0$. Thus the full characteristic cycle detects a failure of flatness that the rank does not detect.
head: environment

label: ex:curve-torsion
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:curve-torsion}
Let $B=\mathbb C[b_1,b_2]$, $J=(b_1,b_2)$, and $M=B[x]\otimes_BJ$, with the usual differential action on $B[x]$. The module is torsion-free over $B$ and has relative characteristic support in the zero section for the order filtration. Its fibers are one copy of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb A^n}$ off the origin and two copies at the origin. For the curve $b_1=t^a$, $b_2=t^b$, with $a,b>0$, the presentation with relation $b_2e_1-b_1e_2=0$ gives
\[
J\otimes_BR\simeq R\oplus R/(t^{\min(a,b)}),
\quad R=\mathbb C[t]_{(t)}.
\]
Thus $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,\mathbb C)\simeq\mathbb C[x]$, and the characteristic cycle gains one copy of the zero section. Torsion-freeness over the parameter plane does not imply torsion-freeness after restriction to a curve through its nonflat point.
head: environment

label: prop:dense-open
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\mathscr M=\operatorname{Rees}_FM$ and $G=\operatorname{gr}_FM$. The $B$-algebra $W_B$ is finitely presented and Noetherian, and $G$ is a finitely presented $W_B$-module. Generic freeness \cite[Tag~051S]{Stacks} gives a nonzero $f_0\in B$ for which $G_{f_0}$ is free, hence flat, over $B_{f_0}$.

For $b\in\operatorname{Spec} B_{f_0}$, tensor the exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathscr M\xrightarrow{\ h\ }\mathscr M\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow0
\]
with $\kappa(b)$. The vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}_1^{B_{f_0}}(G_{f_0},\kappa(b))$ implies that $h$ is injective on $\mathscr M\otimes_B\kappa(b)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:basechange} now gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:generic-gr-fiber}
G\otimes_B\kappa(b)\simeq\operatorname{gr}_F(M_b).
\end{equation}
The same identity holds over $K$. We next compare the lengths at the primes $P_i$ in the generic and special fibers.

Choose a finite prime filtration of $G$ whose successive quotients are of the form $W_B/\mathfrak r_j$ \cite[Tag~00L0]{Stacks}. Every $\mathfrak r_j$ contains some $P_iW_B$, by \eqref{eq:product-support}. Apply generic freeness to the finitely many factors, and shrink the open set so that all surviving factors are flat over the parameter ring. The filtration then remains exact after passage to every fiber over that open set. We now compute the contribution of each factor to the multiplicities.

If $\mathfrak r_j\cap B\ne0$, invert a nonzero element of this intersection; the factor disappears. If $\mathfrak r_j=P_iW_B$, the factor contributes one at $P_i$ in every fiber and zero at the other component primes. Consider the remaining case
\[
P_iW_B\subsetneq\mathfrak r_j.
\]
Choose $g\in\mathfrak r_j\setminus P_iW_B$. Its nonzero image in $(W/P_i)\otimes_\mathbb C B$ can be written
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coefficients}
\overline g=\sum_{a=1}^m c_a\otimes b_a,
\end{equation}
where the $c_a\in W/P_i$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb C$ and some $b_a$ is nonzero. Invert one such $b_a$. At every closed point of the resulting open set, \eqref{eq:coefficients} remains nonzero. Thus $g_b\notin P_i$, so the factor has zero localization at $P_i$ in that fiber. For $k\ne i$, choose $p\in P_i\setminus P_k$. This element annihilates the factor and becomes a unit at $P_k$, so its localization at $P_k$ also vanishes. The same reasoning applies to its generic fiber.

Since the prime filtration has finitely many factors, we may make all these localizations of $B$ simultaneously. On the resulting open set, the length at $P_i$ equals the number of factors isomorphic to $W_B/P_iW_B$ in the prime filtration. This count is the same in each closed fiber and in the generic fiber. Combining it with \eqref{eq:generic-gr-fiber} proves \eqref{eq:dense-open-constant}.
head: environment

label: cor:finite-strata
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:finite-strata}
There is a finite partition of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ into locally closed algebraic strata on which all the functions $\mu_i(M_b)$ are constant. On every irreducible subvariety of the parameter space, the generic multiplicity vector equals the vector on a nonempty open subset of that subvariety.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Closed fibers are unchanged when $B$ is replaced by its reduction. For each irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec} B_{\mathrm{red}}$, apply Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-open} after pullback to that component. By deleting its intersections with the other components, the resulting open subsets may be chosen disjoint. Their complement is a closed set of strictly smaller dimension. Repeat the construction on that complement. There are only finitely many irreducible components at each stage, and dimension decreases, so the process terminates. Lemma~\ref{lem:basechange} preserves \eqref{eq:product-support} at every pullback. The final assertion is Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-open} applied to the chosen irreducible subvariety.
head: environment

label: lem:curve-selection
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:curve-selection}
Let $Y$ be a positive-dimensional irreducible complex algebraic variety, let $U\subseteq Y$ be nonempty and open, and let $y\in Y$ be a closed point. There is an irreducible algebraic curve through $y$ that meets $U$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Work in an affine neighborhood of $y$ and replace $U$ by its intersection with that neighborhood. By Noether normalization \cite[Tag~00OW]{Stacks}, there is a finite morphism $\pi:Y\to\mathbb A^m$, where $m=\dim Y$. The image of $Y\setminus U$ is closed and has dimension smaller than $m$. Choose a line through $\pi(y)$ not contained in this image. Its inverse image is cut out by $m-1$ equations. The height theorem gives a component through $y$ of dimension at least one, and finiteness of $\pi$ gives dimension at most one. Its reduced structure is a curve mapping onto the line, so it meets $U$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-strata}, partition the parameter space into finitely many irreducible locally closed strata $S_\alpha$ on which the multiplicity vector is constant. Fix $i$ and an integer $r$, and let $S_\alpha$ be a stratum on which $\mu_i\ge r$. We show that the same inequality holds at every closed point $b_0\in\overline{S_\alpha}$.

If $\overline{S_\alpha}$ has dimension zero, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, $S_\alpha$ is a nonempty open subset of its irreducible closure. By Lemma~\ref{lem:curve-selection}, there is an irreducible curve through $b_0$ that meets $S_\alpha$. Normalize the curve and choose a closed point over $b_0$. The local ring $R$ at this point is a discrete valuation ring, with residue field $\mathbb C$. Its generic point maps to $S_\alpha$.

Give $M_R=M\otimes_BR$ the induced filtration. By Lemma~\ref{lem:basechange}, the product support condition holds for $M_R$. The generic multiplicity vector on the curve equals the constant vector on $S_\alpha$, because Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-open} gives equality on a nonempty open subset of the curve meeting $S_\alpha$. Theorem~\ref{thm:curve} therefore yields
\[
\mu_i(M_{b_0})\ge\mu_i((M_R)_K)=\mu_i(M_b)\ge r
\quad(b\in S_\alpha).
\]
It follows that, on closed points, the upper level set is
\[
\{b:\mu_i(M_b)\ge r\}
=\bigcup_{\alpha:\,\mu_i|_{S_\alpha}\ge r}\overline{S_\alpha}
\]
This is a finite union of Zariski closed sets, proving upper semicontinuity.
head: environment

label: cor:generic-min
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:generic-min}
If $B$ is a domain and $K=\operatorname{Frac} B$, then $\mu_i(M_b)\ge\mu_i(M_K)$ at every closed point $b$. If the family is flat over a smooth curve, the multiplicity vector is constant on that curve.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For the first assertion, use the dense open subset of Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-open} and upper semicontinuity. For the second, apply Corollary~\ref{cor:flat-curve} at every closed point of the curve.
head: environment

label: prop:positive-functional
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:positive-functional}
Let $L_1,\ldots,L_m$ be fixed projective weights such that the same finite $D_B$-module $M$ satisfies \eqref{eq:product-support} for each weight, with a possibly different fixed set of components. Let $\Phi$ be a fixed integer linear combination of the corresponding multiplicities. Suppose that $\Phi(\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,k))\ge0$ for every DVR arising from pullback along a parameter curve. Then $b\mapsto\Phi(M_b)$ is Zariski upper semicontinuous and constant on a finite algebraic stratification.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take a common refinement of the finitely many stratifications from Theorem~\ref{thm:general}. On each stratum the expression $\Phi(M_b)$ is constant. On a parameter curve, applying Theorem~\ref{thm:curve} at each weight and taking the indicated combination gives
\[
\Phi(M_0)-\Phi(M_{\mathrm{gen}})=\Phi\bigl(\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,k)\bigr)\ge0.
\]
The same unfiltered Tor module occurs at every weight. Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-open} identifies the generic cycle expression with the value at general complex fibers. The curve-selection argument in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:general} now shows that every superlevel set of $\Phi$ is closed.
head: environment

label: def:orbit-conormal
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Conormals to torus orbits

label: def:umbrella
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:umbrella}
Let $L=(u,v)$ be a rational projective weight. Consider the points $[1:0]$ and $[v_j:a_j]$ in $\mathbb P^d(\mathbb R)$. Since the cone of $A$ is pointed and its columns are nonzero, there is a rational linear form $\ell$ positive on every $a_j$. For a sufficiently small positive rational $\varepsilon$, the functional
\[
(t,a)\longmapsto\varepsilon t+\ell(a)
\]
is positive on the displayed representatives. Normalize all representatives to the affine hyperplane $\varepsilon t+\ell(a)=1$ and take their convex hull. The \emph{$(A,L)$-umbrella} $\Phi_A^L$ consists of its faces not containing $[1:0]$, labeled by all the columns lying on a face, and includes the empty face.
head: environment
name: $(A,L)$-umbrella

title: Proof
body_md:
We first reduce to the case $\mathbb Z A=\mathbb Z^d$. If $\mathbb Z A$ is a proper sublattice of $\mathbb Z^d$, choose a basis of $\mathbb Z A$ and let $U\in\operatorname{GL}_d(\mathbb Q)$ be the corresponding change-of-basis matrix. Replacing $(A,\beta)$ by $(UA,U\beta)$ preserves the toric ideal and the defining ideal of the hypergeometric module. It also preserves the $(A,L)$-umbrella and the corresponding characteristic cycle multiplicities. Since the induced change of parameters is an algebraic isomorphism, it suffices to consider the case $\mathbb Z A=\mathbb Z^d$.

By right exactness of tensor product, the fiber of $\mathcal M_B$ in \eqref{eq:relative-gkz} at $b=\beta$ is $M_A(\beta)$. The relative module $\mathcal M_B$ satisfies the product support condition \eqref{eq:gkz-product}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:basechange} ensures that the induced filtrations on its fibers are good. By \eqref{eq:cc-length}, the multiplicity along $\Lambda_\tau$ is $\mu_{A,0}^{L,\tau}(\beta)$. Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:general}, we conclude that $\{\beta\in\mathbb C^d:\mu_{A,0}^{L,\tau}(\beta)\ge r\}$ is Zariski closed for every integer $r$, as required.

label: def:euler-koszul
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:euler-koszul}
For a graded $P$-module $N$ and a parameter $\beta\in\mathbb C^d$, the commuting $D$-linear endomorphisms on $D\otimes_PN$ are defined on a homogeneous element $m$ by
\[
(E_i-\beta_i)\circ m=(E_i-\beta_i+\deg_i m)m.
\]
The \emph{Euler--Koszul complex} of $N$ at $\beta$ is the Koszul complex of these endomorphisms. We denote its homology by $H_j(N,\beta)$.
head: environment
name: Euler--Koszul homology

label: def:toric-module
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:toric-module}
A \emph{finite toric module} is a graded $P$-module with a finite filtration whose factors are graded translates of the semigroup rings of faces of $A$.

label: ex:rankjump-seed
title: Example

label: ex:nonconvex-short
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:nonconvex-short}
To obtain a nonconvex example with a parameter jump, let
\[
B_0=\begin{pmatrix}2&0&1\\0&3&1\end{pmatrix},
\quad A_\dagger=B_0\oplus T_0.
\]
The toric ring of $B_0$ is the hypersurface with equation $\partial_1^3\partial_2^2-\partial_3^6$. Its zero-section coefficient is independent of the parameter. Writing $\delta(v)=6v_3-3v_1-2v_2$, the coefficient equals five for $\delta(v)\le0$ and six for $\delta(v)>0$. Indeed, the two umbrella edges in the first open region give normalized areas $2+3$, while the other open region gives six. On the wall, the formula in \cite[Theorem~4.21]{SW08} subtracts the area of $\operatorname{conv}((2,0),(0,3),(1,1))$ from that of $\operatorname{conv}(0,(2,0),(0,3),(1,1))$, giving $6-1=5$.

Take $v=(2,3,1,1,1,1,1)$ and $u=4\mathbf1-v$. In the $B_0$ face the unscaled triangles contain $(2,0)$ and $(0,3)$ but not their midpoint, so this weight is nonconvex in the sense of \cite[Section~6]{BFF20}. The presentation as an external product, together with the tensor-product filtration, gives
\[
\mu_{A_\dagger,0}^{L,\varnothing}(\beta)
=5\bigl(4+\mathbf 1_{\{\beta_3=1,\,\beta_4=2\}}(\beta)\bigr).
\]
Thus the multiplicity increases from $20$ to $25$ on the indicated parameter plane. By Corollary~\ref{cor:gkz-curve}, this increase equals the coefficient of the zero section in the characteristic cycle of the Tor module. The matrix $B_0$ has column lattice $\mathbb Z^2$, so the normalized areas here use the intrinsic column lattice.
head: environment

label: def:gevrey-irregularity
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:gevrey-irregularity}
Let $s\ge1$ and let $\sum_{m\ge0}f_m(x')x_n^m$ be a formal series with holomorphic coefficients on $Y$. It has \emph{Gevrey order at most $s$} if the series $\sum_{m\ge0}f_m(x')x_n^m/(m!)^{s-1}$ converges locally. The sheaf of such series is denoted by $\mathcal O_{\widehat{X|Y}}(s)$; at $s=1$ it is the sheaf of convergent germs along $Y$.

For a holonomic $D$-module $N$ and $s>1$, the \emph{irregularity complex of order $s$} and its generic degree-zero rank are
\[
I_s(N)=\mathbf R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}}\bigl(N^{\mathrm{an}},
\mathcal O_{\widehat{X|Y}}(s)/\mathcal O_{X|Y}\bigr),
\quad d_s(N)=\operatorname{rank}_Y\mathcal H^0 I_s(N).
\]
The rank is computed at a general point of $Y$.
head: environment
name: Gevrey series and irregularity

label: def:gevrey-graded
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:gevrey-graded}
Let $N$ be holonomic, and let $1<a<b$ be non-slope levels. We denote by $e_{a,b}(N)$ the generic dimension along $Y$ of
\[
\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}}\bigl(N^{\mathrm{an}},
\mathcal O_{\widehat{X|Y}}(b)/\mathcal O_{\widehat{X|Y}}(a)\bigr).
\]
For $\rho>1$, choose non-slope levels $1<a<\rho<b$ such that $[a,b]$ contains no slope of $N$ other than possibly $\rho$. We write $e_\rho(N)=e_{a,b}(N)$ for the generic dimension of the graded piece of the Gevrey filtration at $\rho$.
head: environment

label: lem:index
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We apply the Gevrey index theorem with the following conventions. Laurent--Mebkhout \cite[Theorem~2.3.1 and \S2.4]{LM99}, using the positivity theorem of Mebkhout \cite{Meb90}, prove that the irregularity complexes with their Gevrey maps form an increasing filtration in the abelian category of perverse sheaves; the graded objects are perverse as well. With the usual middle-perversity convention of \cite{BBD82,KS90}, in which a local system on the smooth $(n-1)$-fold $Y$ is shifted by $n-1$, the complexes here are $I_s(N)[n-1]$. The unshifted convention in \eqref{eq:irregularity} is the one used for the degree-zero ranks in \cite[\S7]{BFF20}. On a dense open subset of $Y$, each unshifted irregularity complex and each unshifted graded complex has cohomology only in degree zero. Consequently, its generic Euler characteristic equals the nonnegative dimension of its degree-zero cohomology.

The index formula uses the conventions for characteristic cycles and Euler obstructions in microlocal index theory \cite{Kas85,KS90}. We specify the sign for the Gevrey formula of \cite{LM99}. In coordinates $(x',y;\xi',\eta)$, the symplectic identification with the cotangent bundle of $\Lambda=T_Y^*X$ is
\[
(x',y;\xi',\eta)\longmapsto(x',\eta;\xi',-y).
\]
It is the identification used for $(F,V_Y)$ in \cite[Remark~3.3]{SW08}. We distinguish two numerical conventions for slopes. On p.~57 of \cite{LM99}, a rational level $r=p/q>1$ defines the filtration $qF+(p-q)V_Y=qL(r)$. Its weight on $y^l\partial_y^k\partial_{x'}^\alpha$ is $p(k-l)+q(l+|\alpha|)$. Thus the Gevrey level in this paper is exactly the parameter in that filtration. The microlocal type in \cite[Remark~3.3]{SW08} for $aF+bV_Y$ is $1+a/b$; for our $L(r)$ that label is $r/(r-1)$, whereas the Gevrey order is $r$. The zero section of $T^*X$ becomes the conormal of the zero section $Y\subset\Lambda$, while $C_Y$ becomes the zero section of $T^*\Lambda$. The Euler-obstruction signs of these two cycles at a general point of $Y\subset\Lambda$ are respectively $-1$ and $+1$. The index formula for formal completion in \cite[p.~64, immediately before \S2.4]{LM99} has the additional minus sign. Consequently the generic index for solutions with values in a Gevrey completion at a non-slope level is $m_Z^r-m_Y^r$.

At a general point of $Y$, only these two components contribute. At a bihomogeneous level the cycles are conormal cycles. If the irreducible base of another conormal in $T^*\Lambda$ contained the zero section $Y\subset\Lambda$, dimension would force that base to be $Y$ or $\Lambda$. All other bases meet $Y$ in proper closed subsets, which can be avoided in computing the generic index. 

The index at the convergent level is $\phi_{r_0}$. At a finite Gevrey level $s$, the index is $\phi_{r_+}$: the one-sided convention follows from the open and closed Gevrey levels in \cite[Theorem~2.3.1]{LM99}. In particular a slope equal to $s$ is included. The same convention is used in \cite[equation~(7-1)]{BFF20}. The short exact sequence defining the quotient by convergent series gives \eqref{eq:G} as a difference of the two indices. Since the cohomology is generically concentrated in degree zero, this difference equals $d_s(N)$.

For \eqref{eq:grade}, the exact sequence of coefficient sheaves gives the distinguished triangle
\[
I_a(N)\longrightarrow I_b(N)\longrightarrow
\mathbf R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}}\bigl(N^{\mathrm{an}},\mathcal O_{\widehat{X|Y}}(b)/\mathcal O_{\widehat{X|Y}}(a)\bigr)\xrightarrow{+1}.
\]
The first arrow, shifted by $n-1$, is a monomorphism in the perverse category by the theorem on the Gevrey filtration just cited. Its cone is the perverse quotient. On a common dense open subset of $Y$ this is an exact sequence of local systems, unshifted to degree zero. Taking their dimensions proves \eqref{eq:grade} and identifies its left side with the ordinary $\mathcal Hom$ in the statement.
head: environment

label: lem:tor-control
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tor-control}
Under \eqref{eq:gevrey-support}--\eqref{eq:gevrey-bihom}, for any pullback to a DVR $R$ associated with a parameter curve, the module
\[
T=\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M_R,k)=\ker(t:M_R\to M_R)
\]
is a finite holonomic $D$-module. All complex fibers and $T$ have analytic slopes along $Y$ in $\Sigma$, and satisfy Lemma~\ref{lem:index} with the same choices of levels.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The ring $D_R$ is Noetherian, so the kernel is finite over $D_R$. It is killed by $t$, hence finite over $D_R/(t)\simeq D$. For each weight use the induced filtration on this kernel. The associated graded module injects into the associated graded module of the curve family; its support is contained in the special slice of the prescribed product support. The support condition for the order filtration shows that $T$ is holonomic.

Every irreducible component of the characteristic variety of a finite $D$-module for a projective filtration has dimension at least $n$ by \cite[Theorem~3.2]{SW08}. A closed subset with this property in a finite union of irreducible $n$-dimensional varieties is a union of some of those varieties. Hence, for $r\notin\Sigma$, the characteristic variety of $T$ is bihomogeneous. The same argument applies to each fiber, using the surjection \eqref{eq:basechange-surj} for the induced filtration. There is no algebraic slope at such $r$. The analytic and algebraic slopes coincide by \cite[Theorem~2.4.2]{LM99}. Thus the analytic slopes of $T$ and of all fibers lie in $\Sigma$.
head: environment

label: thm:gevrey-general
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose one rational representative of every component of $(1,\infty)\setminus\Sigma$. For a given $s$, choose the representative immediately to the right of $s$ or in its interval, and the representative next to $1$. For a given $\rho>1$, choose representatives on both sides; equivalently, first take $a=\rho-\epsilon$ and $b=\rho+\epsilon$ with rational $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small. These choices have the same graded dimension. This is a finite list independent of the fiber and of the parameter curve. Lemmas~\ref{lem:index} and~\ref{lem:tor-control} express all the relevant invariants as fixed linear combinations at these weights, both for complex fibers and for $T$. Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:curve} gives \eqref{eq:Gtor} and \eqref{eq:Etor}. These invariants are generic dimensions of an irregularity object or its perverse graded quotient, and are therefore nonnegative. Proposition~\ref{prop:positive-functional} completes the proof.

For $s$ below every member of $\Sigma$, the two cycle expressions agree and $d_s=0$. For $\rho\notin\Sigma$, choose both levels in the same interval; the graded object vanishes. The first slope and several changes at the same slope are handled by the same quotient. All facets changing at a repeated slope contribute to that one object. For each comparison only finitely many modules occur, and their generic-open subsets of $Y$ have a common dense open intersection.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:gkz-product}, the cyclic family \eqref{eq:relative-gkz} satisfies \eqref{eq:gevrey-support} for every projective weight. Along $L(r)$ there are finitely many umbrella walls. They can also be read from the finitely many supporting hyperplanes of $\operatorname{conv}(0,a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1})$ not passing through the origin: the possible changes occur when $a_n/r$ meets one of them; degenerate cases can be read directly from the finite rational fan of initial ideals. The walls are rational. Away them the umbrella components are $(F,V_Y)$-bihomogeneous, as in the slope criterion of \cite[Corollary~4.18]{SW08} and \cite[Remark~7.1]{BFF20}. Thus \eqref{eq:gevrey-support}--\eqref{eq:gevrey-bihom} hold. Theorem~\ref{thm:gevrey-general} proves both assertions.

By the right-hand convention, the rational representatives compute the specified Gevrey level even when that level is a slope. The support theorem applies equally to nonconvex weights and to ties.
head: environment

label: ex:pressure
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:pressure}
Consider the family
\[
M=D_{\mathbb A^1}[t]/D_{\mathbb A^1}[t](x^2\partial-t).
\]
As a left $D$-module, $M$ is isomorphic to $D$, with the central parameter $t$ acting by right multiplication by $x^2\partial$. A nonzero polynomial in this operator is nonzero, by its highest order symbol, and the Weyl algebra is a domain. Thus $M$ is torsion-free, and hence flat, over $\mathbb C[t]$ and its localization at $(t)$.

For $t\ne0$ the connection off $x=0$ has solution $\exp(-t/x)$ and slope $2$. Its generic irregularity along the point is $1$ for $s\geq2$ and $0$ below $2$. At $t=0$, the quotient $D/D(x^2\partial)$ is regular: factorization gives an extension with factors $D/D\partial$ and $D/Dx^2$, the latter supported at the point. Its irregularity is zero at all levels. For the order filtration, both fibers have characteristic cycle $[Z]+2[T_0^*\mathbb A^1]$.

For the filtrations needed in Theorem~\ref{thm:gevrey-general}, the relative principal symbol is
\[
\begin{cases}
x^2\xi,&1<r<2,\\
x^2\xi-t,&r=2,\\
t,&r>2.
\end{cases}
\]
At $r=2$ it defines moving curves rather than a finite union of fixed curves times the parameter line. At $r>2$ its special support is the whole two-dimensional cotangent space, not a union of fixed one-dimensional components. Thus the support conditions for $L(r)$ fail, while the condition for the order filtration holds, in agreement with Corollary~\ref{cor:flatness}.
head: environment

label: ex:multiple-slopes
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:multiple-slopes}
We consider two normal configurations in which the relevant facets contribute at distinct slopes or at the same slope. Let
\[
A=(e_1,e_2,(4,0),(3,2),(0,4),a_6),\quad Y=\{x_6=0\}.
\]
Its semigroup is $\mathbb N^2$, so the relevant characteristic cycles and irregularities are constant in the parameter. The two facets of $\operatorname{conv}(0,A\setminus\{a_6\})$ not through zero have supporting forms $(1/4,1/8)$ and $(1/6,1/4)$, and normalized triangle volumes $8$ and $12$. If $a_6=(8,8)$, the slopes are $3$ and $10/3$, and $d_s$ is $0$, $8$, and $20$ on $1<s<3$, $3\leq s<10/3$, and $s\geq10/3$, respectively. Thus the two graded dimensions are $8$ and $12$. If $a_6=(9,6)$, both facets change at $3$, and the one graded dimension there is $20$. Since $a_6/3=(3,2)$, both facets adjacent to $(3,2)$ contribute to the jump at $s=3$. The generic formula \cite[equation~(7-2)]{BFF20}, together with the Cohen--Macaulay property, proves these statements for all parameters.
head: environment

label: def:exceptional-arrangement
title: Definition
head: environment

label: def:partial-saturation
title: Definition
head: environment

label: prop:ext-inclusion
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ext-inclusion}
For every $s>1$ and every individual level $\rho>1$,
\[
\{\beta:d_s(M_A(\beta))>d_s(A)\}\subseteq\mathcal Z(S_A^{\{n\}}).
\]
The analogous inclusion holds for a graded dimension exceeding its generic value. If $S_A^{\{n\}}$ is Cohen--Macaulay, all these generic dimensions are constant in $\beta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $N=S_A^{\{n\}}$ and $Q=N/S_A$. Since $N$ is finite and embeds in $S_A[\partial_n^{-1}]$, one power of $\partial_n$ kills $Q$. A finite toric filtration of $Q$ has factors which are translates of $S_G$ with $a_n\notin G$. Indeed, if $a_n\in G$, multiplication by $\partial_n$ is injective on $S_G$, contradicting its nilpotence on the factor.

For each such factor, the Euler--Koszul complex is the external product of a complex in the variables indexed by $G$ with $\mathcal O$ in the inactive variables, including $x_n$. This follows directly from $D\otimes_P S_G$: after the degree correction in the Euler endomorphisms, the inactive variables have no Euler action. Its homology is noncharacteristic for $Y$ and has zero irregularity along $Y$ at every level. The exactness of the irregularity functor in the perverse category makes this vanishing stable under subquotients and extensions. Induction on the toric filtration, using the long exact sequences in Euler--Koszul homology, shows that every $H_i(Q,\beta)$ has zero irregularity. Consequently $H_0(S_A,\beta)$ and $H_0(N,\beta)$ have the same irregularity objects, and therefore the same generic graded dimensions, for every $\beta$.

Off $\mathcal Z(N)$ the higher Euler--Koszul homology of $N$ is zero. Its Euler characteristic cycle is independent of $\beta$ by \cite[Theorem~4.11]{SW08}. It equals that of $S_A$: the quotient $Q$ has a filtration by modules associated with proper faces, and each such factor has an exterior Euler factor $(1-1)^{\operatorname{codim}G}=0$. Thus $H_0(N,\beta)$ has the generic characteristic coefficients of $S_A$ off $\mathcal Z(N)$, at every weight used in Lemma~\ref{lem:index}. This proves the inclusions and the Cohen--Macaulay implication.
head: environment

label: rem:shift
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:shift}
The Ext expression in \cite[Conjecture~7.10]{BFF20} is written with a shift $-\varepsilon_A$. With the convention $N(b)_v=N_{v-b}$, graded local duality instead takes the form \eqref{eq:exceptional}. For example, $\operatorname{Ext}_P^n(\mathbb C(b),P)$ has generator degree $-b-\varepsilon_A$. We use the canonical-module expression throughout. The counterexample below has an empty Gevrey jump locus and a nonempty exceptional arrangement, so the failure of equality persists under either fixed translation.
head: environment

label: thm:counterexample
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: eq:SA-presentation
title: Proof
body_md:
Use $T_0$ and its hole $b$ from Example~\ref{ex:rankjump-seed}. The fifth and sixth columns in \eqref{eq:AK} are redundant generators $3a_1$ and $3a_4$. In a semigroup algebra introduce $z$ of degree $(0,0,1)$, let $m\in S_{T_0}$ be the monomial of degree $(2,4)$, and put $q=mz$ and $w=z^K$. There is an isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:SA-presentation}
S:=S_{A_K}=S_{T_0}[w,q]/(q^K-m^K w).
\end{equation}
Indeed, division by the monic relation gives a spanning set $1,q,\ldots,q^{K-1}$ over $S_{T_0}[w]$. These terms have distinct $z$-exponents modulo $K$, so they are independent in the semigroup algebra. Equivalently, the degree set consists exactly of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:degrees-S}
(u+j(2,4),\ j+K\ell),\quad u\in\mathbb N T_0,\quad 0\leq j<K,\quad\ell\geq0.
\end{equation}
Saturating by the last column permits $\ell\in\mathbb Z$. Intersecting with the cone forces $j+K\ell\geq0$, hence $\ell\geq0$. This proves $S^{\{8\}}=S$.

Consider the finite toric module
\[
N=\widetilde S_{T_0}[w,q]/(q^K-m^K w).
\]
It is free with basis $1,q,\ldots,q^{K-1}$ over the Cohen--Macaulay ring $\widetilde S_{T_0}[w]$, and is therefore Cohen--Macaulay of dimension $3$. The quotient is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:QK}
Q=N/S\simeq \bigl(\mathbb C[q,w]/(q^K)\bigr)(b,0),
\quad \deg q=(2,4,1),\quad\deg w=(0,0,K).
\end{equation}
Every positive monomial of $S_{T_0}$ kills its unique normalization hole. This proves that the first six differential variables act by zero in \eqref{eq:QK}, while multiplication by $q$ advances the residue $j$ until the last step, where multiplication by $m^K w$ kills the hole. These actions determine the displayed module isomorphism.

The quotient $Q$ has both depth and dimension $1$: it is free over $\mathbb C[w]$ of rank $K$ and $q$ is nilpotent. The depth lemma \cite[Chapter~1]{BH98}, applied to $0\to S\to N\to Q\to0$, gives $\operatorname{depth} S=2$. Since $N$ has no local cohomology in degrees below $3$, this sequence also gives
\[
H^0_{\mathfrak m}(S)=H^1_{\mathfrak m}(S)=0,
\quad H^2_{\mathfrak m}(S)\simeq H^1_{\mathfrak m}(Q).
\]
Since the radical of the positive ideal on $Q$ is $(q,w)$ and $q$ is nilpotent, we have $H^1_{\mathfrak m}(Q)=Q_w/Q$. Its degrees are
\[
b_j-\ell a_8,\quad b_j=(1+2j,2+4j,j),\quad 0\leq j<K,\quad\ell\geq1.
\]
Their Zariski closure is exactly \eqref{eq:ZK}. We can also verify this using Ext. Put $b_0=(1,2,0)$, $J=(\partial_1,\ldots,\partial_6,\partial_7^K)\subset P$, and $\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^6a_i+Ka_7$. Then $Q=(P/J)(b_0)$ is a complete intersection module. Since $N$ is Cohen--Macaulay of dimension $3$ over the regular ring $P$ of dimension $8$, the Auslander--Buchsbaum formula \cite[Chapter~1]{BH98} gives projective dimension $5$. The Ext long exact sequence gives
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_P^6(S,P)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_P^7(Q,P)
\simeq(P/J)(-b_0-\Delta),
\]
and the other terms $\operatorname{Ext}_P^{8-q}(S,P)$ for $q<3$ vanish. This follows from the graded Koszul resolution of the displayed seven generators of $J$, with the grading of the canonical module as in \cite[Chapter~3]{BH98}. Using $\omega_P=P(\varepsilon_A)$ and negating the resulting quasidegrees gives precisely \eqref{eq:ZK}, in agreement with the calculation using local cohomology.

We next compute the Euler--Koszul homology of $Q$. The filtration of $Q$ by powers of $q$ has factors $\mathbb C[w](b_j)$. Their Euler--Koszul homology vanishes unless $\beta\in b_j+\mathbb C a_8$. On this line, the homology in degree $i$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Qhom}
\mathcal O_{\mathbb A^7}\boxtimes
D_8/D_8\bigl(Kx_8\partial_8-(\beta_3-j)\bigr)
\otimes_\mathbb C\bigwedge^i\mathbb C^2.
\end{equation}
The two Euler directions that act trivially give the exterior factor. The lines have different first two coordinates. Hence, at any parameter, at most one filtration factor has nonzero homology; all other factors are acyclic. The long exact sequences then give \eqref{eq:Qhom} for $H_i(Q,\beta)$ on the relevant line, and zero off their union. The Kummer module in \eqref{eq:Qhom} is regular along $x_8=0$ for every parameter, including integral ones. Its meromorphic connection has a logarithmic pole, as in the theory of regular singular connections \cite[Chapter~II]{Del70}; point-supported subquotients at integral exponents remain regular in the holonomic category \cite[Chapter~5]{HTT08}. Therefore $I_s(H_i(Q,\beta))=0$ for all $i,s,\beta$.


Since $N$ is Cohen--Macaulay, its higher Euler--Koszul homology modules vanish for all $\beta$ by \cite[Theorem~6.6]{MMW05}. Consequently, $\operatorname{CC}^L(H_0(N,\beta))$ equals the Euler characteristic cycle of the Euler--Koszul complex, which is independent of $\beta$ by \cite[Theorem~4.11]{SW08}. This holds for every projective weight $L$, including $L(r)$. The long exact sequence in Euler--Koszul homology for $0\to S\to N\to Q\to0$, together with the regularity just proved, implies
\[
I_s(H_0(S,\beta))\simeq I_s(H_0(N,\beta))
\]
for every parameter. Since $N/S$ has smaller dimension, the constant Euler cycle of $N$ is the generic cycle of $S$. Thus it remains to compute the generic irregularity.

The columns of $T_0$ generate $\mathbb Z^2$, and $a_7$ differs from an element of their semigroup by $(0,0,1)$; hence $\mathbb Z A_K=\mathbb Z^3$. The cone is the product of the pointed cone of $T_0$ with the positive third ray. After deleting $a_8$, the polytope is the simplex with vertices $0,p_*,q_*,c_*$, where
\[
p_*=(3,0,0),\quad q_*=(3,12,0),\quad c_*=(2,4,1).
\]
Its only facet not through zero is supported by $\ell(x,y,z)=(x+z)/3=1$. The moving point $a_8/r$ meets that plane exactly at $r=K/3$. Before this value $c_*$ is inside $\operatorname{conv}(0,p_*,q_*,a_8/r)$, since its barycentric coefficients are $1/3,1/3,r/K$ and have sum below $1$. After this value the new facet not containing $a_8$ is $\{p_*,q_*,c_*\}$. The generic Gevrey formula \cite[equation~(7-2)]{BFF20} therefore gives its normalized volume
\[
|\det(p_*,q_*,c_*)|=36.
\]
At the wall, this contribution is counted at $s=K/3$, according to the convention used above. The slope criterion of \cite[Corollary~4.18]{SW08} proves that $K/3$ is the sole slope. This proves \eqref{eq:constant-irreg}.
head: environment

label: prop:CM-cover
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The higher homology of $N$ vanishes. Split
\[
0\to H_1(Q,\beta)\to H_0(S_A,\beta)\to H_0(N,\beta)\to H_0(Q,\beta)\to0
\]
into two short exact sequences and apply the additivity of generic irregularity. The constant Euler cycle of $N$ is the generic cycle of $S_A$, as in the proof above. Graded dimensions are differences of two additive generic irregularities, so the same identity holds for them. The curve assertion is Theorem~\ref{thm:gevrey-general}.
